claim: The CRISPR-Cas9 bacterial surveillance system has become a versatile tool for genome editing and gene regulation in eukaryotic cells.
source: The CRISPR-Cas9 bacterial surveillance system has become a versatile tool for genome editing and gene regulation in eukaryotic cells, yet how CRISPR-Cas9 contends with the barriers presented by eukaryotic chromatin is poorly understood.
evidence: This is supported by references to established applications in the field and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Nucleosomes assembled on native DNA sequences are permissive to Cas9 action.
source: We find that nucleosomes assembled on native DNA sequences are permissive to Cas9 action.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing Cas9 activity on 5S nucleosomes versus 601 nucleosomes shown in Figure 2.

claim: The accessibility of nucleosomal DNA to Cas9 is variable over several orders of magnitude depending on dynamic properties of the DNA sequence and the distance of the PAM site from the nucleosome dyad.
source: However, the accessibility of nucleosomal DNA to Cas9 is variable over several orders of magnitude depending on dynamic properties of the DNA sequence and the distance of the PAM site from the nucleosome dyad.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing different cleavage rates at different positions within nucleosomes (Figure 1D, Figure 2D).

claim: Chromatin remodeling enzymes stimulate Cas9 activity on nucleosomal templates.
source: We further find that chromatin remodeling enzymes stimulate Cas9 activity on nucleosomal templates.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing enhanced Cas9 cleavage in the presence of SNF2h and RSC remodelers (Figure 3).

claim: The spontaneous breathing of nucleosomal DNA together with the action of chromatin remodelers allow Cas9 to effectively act on chromatin in vivo.
source: Our findings imply that the spontaneous breathing of nucleosomal DNA together with the action of chromatin remodelers allow Cas9 to effectively act on chromatin in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the biochemical data presented and extrapolated to in vivo conditions.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 originated in bacteria, where genomic DNA generally consists of supercoiled circular molecules associated with nucleoid-associated proteins.
source: CRISPR-Cas9 originated in bacteria, where genomic DNA generally consists of supercoiled circular molecules associated with nucleoid-associated proteins (Travers and Muskhelishvili, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established knowledge about bacterial DNA organization.

claim: Eukaryotic chromosomes are linear, packaged with histone octamers into nucleosomes, and further organized into higher-order structures.
source: In contrast, eukaryotic chromosomes are linear, packaged with histone octamers into nucleosomes, and further organized into higher-order structures (Luger et al., 1997; Olins and Olins, 1974; Woodcock et al., 1976; Dixon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to foundational work on chromatin structure.

claim: The packaging of DNA into nucleosomes generally inhibits the binding of sequence specific DNA binding factors.
source: The packaging of DNA into nucleosomes generally inhibits the binding of sequence specific DNA binding factors.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the chromatin field.

claim: ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers reposition, remove, or restructure nucleosomes to regulate the access of DNA binding factors.
source: Further, in eukaryotes ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers reposition, remove, or restructure nucleosomes to regulate the access of DNA binding factors (Clapier and Cairns, 2009; Narlikar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles on chromatin remodeling.

claim: The Widom 601 sequence is an artificially derived sequence with high affinity for the histone octamer.
source: The 601 sequence is an artificially derived sequence with high affinity for the histone octamer and has proved a valuable tool for assembling well positioning nucleosomes for biochemical studies.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the 601 sequence, supported by citation (Lowary and Widom, 1998).

claim: Targeting DNA flanking the nucleosome showed cleavage rates comparable to those of naked DNA.
source: Targeting the DNA flanking the nucleosome showed cleavage rates comparable to those of naked DNA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cleavage rates at entry/exit sites of the nucleosome were much lower compared to naked DNA (~23–28x decrease cleavage rate vs. DNA alone).
source: Cleavage rates at entry/exit sites of the nucleosome were much lower compared to naked DNA (~23–28x decrease cleavage rate vs. DNA alone) (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and quantification shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: Targeting near the nucleosomal dyad resulted in further inhibition of cutting by Cas9 (~1000x decrease vs. DNA alone).
source: Targeting near the nucleosomal dyad resulted in further inhibition of cutting by Cas9 (~1000x decrease vs. DNA alone) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Nucleosomal DNA transiently disengages from the histone octamer, a process termed as nucleosomal DNA unpeeling or breathing.
source: Previous work has shown that nucleosomal DNA transiently disengages from the histone octamer, a process termed as nucleosomal DNA unpeeling or breathing.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on nucleosome dynamics.

claim: The equilibrium for DNA unpeeling gets progressively more unfavorable the closer the DNA site gets to the dyad.
source: The equilibrium for DNA unpeeling gets progressively more unfavorable the closer the DNA site gets to the dyad (Polach and Widom, 1995; Li and Widom, 2004; Luger et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on nucleosome breathing dynamics.

claim: The nucleosome-mediated inhibition of Cas9 activity is more pronounced near the dyad suggesting that Cas9 cleavage occurs on DNA that is transiently disengaged from the histone octamer.
source: The nucleosome-mediated inhibition of Cas9 activity is more pronounced near the dyad suggesting that Cas9 cleavage occurs on DNA that is transiently disengaged from the histone octamer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing position-dependent inhibition and knowledge of nucleosome breathing.

claim: Cas9 recognizes DNA target sites in a two-step process that begins with binding to the DNA protospacer adjacent motif (PAM, in this case 'NGG') through its C-terminal PAM-interacting region, followed by sequential melting of the DNA double strand and annealing of the sgRNA guide segment to the unwound target DNA strand.
source: Cas9 recognizes DNA target sites in a two-step process that begins with binding to the DNA protospacer adjacent motif (PAM, in this case 'NGG') through its C-terminal PAM-interacting region, followed by sequential melting of the DNA double strand and annealing of the sgRNA guide segment to the unwound target DNA strand (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Sternberg et al., 2014; Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous mechanistic studies and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Complete annealing of the 20-nt guide RNA to the target DNA is required to drive a progressive conformational transformation that authorizes Cas9 to simultaneously cleave both DNA strands.
source: Complete annealing of the 20-nt guide RNA to the target DNA is required to drive a progressive conformational transformation that authorizes Cas9 to simultaneously cleave both DNA strands (Sternberg et al., 2015; Josephs et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous mechanistic studies.

claim: Binding of dCas9 pre-loaded with core targeting sgRNA with 601 0/0 nucleosomes is undetectable whereas binding to naked DNA control is still robust.
source: Binding of dCas9 pre-loaded with core targeting sgRNA with 601 0/0 nucleosomes is undetectable whereas binding to naked DNA control is still robust (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The highly transient dCas9 binding to PAMs within target DNA is observable as super shifts in the gel binding assay.
source: We investigated this further and determined that, in our binding assay, the highly transient dCas9 binding to PAMs within target DNA is observable as super shifts, likely due to a combination of a high number of PAMs on the target DNA (23 NGG PAMs present in 601 0/0 sequence) and common caging effects of gel binding assays.
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental observations from the gel shift assay.

claim: The absence of a super shift binding pattern with 0/0 nucleosomes suggests that dCas9 cannot stably interact with PAMs located on nucleosomes.
source: The absence of a super shift binding pattern with 0/0 nucleosomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, right) suggests that dCas9 cannot stably interact with PAMs located on nucleosomes, in a manner consistent with a recently published study (Hinz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data supported by citation to a consistent study.

claim: The artificial Widom 601 is an atypically strong nucleosome positioning sequence that shows ~100-fold less breathing dynamics compared to physiological nucleosome positioning sequences, such as the 5S rRNA gene.
source: The artificial Widom 601 is an atypically strong nucleosome positioning sequence that shows ~100-fold less breathing dynamics compared to physiological nucleosome positioning sequences, such as the 5S rRNA gene (Anderson et al., 2002; Partensky and Narlikar, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies comparing breathing dynamics.

claim: Cas9-mediated cleavage at sites near the entry/exit of the nucleosome is substantially enhanced (700–fold) with 5S nucleosomes compared to 601 particles.
source: Cas9-mediated cleavage at sites near the entry/exit of the nucleosome is substantially enhanced (700–fold) with 5S nucleosomes compared to 601 particles (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: With 601 nucleosomes, cutting at the entry/exit site is 1000-fold slower than in naked DNA.
source: In the context of 601, cutting at this site is 1000-fold slower than in naked DNA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: With 5S nucleosomes, cutting at the entry/exit site is only 1.5-fold slower than in naked DNA.
source: In contrast, with 5S nucleosomes, cutting at the comparable site is only 1.5-fold slower than in naked DNA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cas9 cleavage near the dyad is inhibited to a similar extent on both 5S and 601 nucleosomes.
source: However, Cas9 cleavage near the dyad is inhibited to a similar extent on both 5S and 601 nucleosomes, showing that the 5S-specific enhancement of Cas9 activity does not extend all the way to the nucleosomal dyad.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Nucleosomal DNA breathing substantially enhances Cas9 binding to nucleosomes.
source: These results support our interpretation that nucleosomal DNA breathing substantially enhances Cas9 binding to nucleosomes and demonstrate that nucleosomal DNA sequence, through its influence on nucleosome stability, can regulate Cas9 activity over a large dynamic range.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental data comparing 5S and 601 nucleosomes.

claim: Nucleosomal DNA sequence, through its influence on nucleosome stability, can regulate Cas9 activity over a large dynamic range.
source: These results support our interpretation that nucleosomal DNA breathing substantially enhances Cas9 binding to nucleosomes and demonstrate that nucleosomal DNA sequence, through its influence on nucleosome stability, can regulate Cas9 activity over a large dynamic range.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing different cleavage rates on 5S versus 601 nucleosomes.

claim: When incubated with 601 80/0 particles, SNF2h promotes sliding of the nucleosome towards the center of the DNA molecule.
source: When incubated with 601 80/0 particles, SNF2h promotes sliding of the nucleosome towards the center of the DNA molecule (Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) (Längst et al., 1999; He et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and citations to previous work.

claim: Remodeling 80/0 nucleosomes by SNF2h resulted in a strong enhancement of Cas9 cleavage to ~34%.
source: Remodeling 80/0 nucleosomes by SNF2h resulted in a strong enhancement of Cas9 cleavage to ~34%, showing that SNF2h slides the nucleosome enough to improve Cas9's accessibility to the target site and that Cas9 is now able to bind and cleave at a higher rate (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: RSC activity dramatically enhances cleavage on 601 80/80 nucleosomes when Cas9 is targeted to the entry site, negating most of the inhibitory influence of the nucleosome on Cas9.
source: We find that RSC activity also dramatically enhances cleavage on 601 80/80 nucleosomes when Cas9 is targeted to the entry site, negating most of the inhibitory influence of the nucleosome on Cas9 (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E-F.

claim: Two different classes of chromatin remodeling enzymes can significantly enhance Cas9 access to DNA targets normally obscured by nucleosomes.
source: These results demonstrate that two different classes of chromatin remodeling enzymes can significantly enhance Cas9 access to DNA targets normally obscured by nucleosomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data with both SNF2h and RSC remodelers shown in Figure 3.

claim: The intrinsic stability of the histone-DNA interactions plays a critical role in regulating the activity of S. pyogenes Cas9.
source: Here we demonstrate, using detailed biochemical studies with a variety of nucleosomal templates, that (i) the intrinsic stability of the histone-DNA interactions, (ii) the location of the target site within the nucleosomes (nucleosome positioning), and (iii) the action of chromatin remodeling enzymes play critical roles in regulating the activity of S. pyogenes Cas9.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: The location of the target site within the nucleosomes (nucleosome positioning) plays a critical role in regulating the activity of S. pyogenes Cas9.
source: Here we demonstrate, using detailed biochemical studies with a variety of nucleosomal templates, that (i) the intrinsic stability of the histone-DNA interactions, (ii) the location of the target site within the nucleosomes (nucleosome positioning), and (iii) the action of chromatin remodeling enzymes play critical roles in regulating the activity of S. pyogenes Cas9.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: The action of chromatin remodeling enzymes plays a critical role in regulating the activity of S. pyogenes Cas9.
source: Here we demonstrate, using detailed biochemical studies with a variety of nucleosomal templates, that (i) the intrinsic stability of the histone-DNA interactions, (ii) the location of the target site within the nucleosomes (nucleosome positioning), and (iii) the action of chromatin remodeling enzymes play critical roles in regulating the activity of S. pyogenes Cas9.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Recent work using nucleosomes assembled on the 601 sequence has led to the qualitatively similar conclusion that nucleosomes are refractory for Cas9 action.
source: Recent work using nucleosomes assembled on the 601 sequence has led to the qualitatively similar conclusion that nucleosomes are refractory for Cas9 action (Hinz et al., 2015; Horlbeck et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Cas9 sites near the entry/exit sites of 5S nucleosomes are cleaved ~700-fold better than the corresponding sites within 601 nucleosomes.
source: We find that Cas9 sites near the entry/exit sites of 5S nucleosomes are cleaved ~700-fold better than the corresponding sites within 601 nucleosomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: DNA breathing occurs at least 100-fold more in 5S nucleosomes than 601 nucleosomes.
source: Given that DNA breathing occurs at least 100-fold more in 5S nucleosomes than 601 nucleosomes we propose that Cas9 gains access to nucleosomal DNA when the DNA is transiently unpeeled from the histone octamer.
evidence: This is based on cited knowledge about nucleosome breathing dynamics.

claim: Cas9 gains access to nucleosomal DNA when the DNA is transiently unpeeled from the histone octamer.
source: Given that DNA breathing occurs at least 100-fold more in 5S nucleosomes than 601 nucleosomes we propose that Cas9 gains access to nucleosomal DNA when the DNA is transiently unpeeled from the histone octamer.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental data and knowledge of nucleosome breathing.

claim: DNA unpeeling up to the dyad is substantially less favored (100-fold) for both the 601 and 5S nucleosomes than DNA unpeeling near their respective entry/exit sites.
source: This is because DNA unpeeling up to the dyad is substantially less favored (100-fold) for both the 601 and 5S nucleosomes than DNA unpeeling near their respective entry/exit sites (Anderson and Widom, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on nucleosome breathing thermodynamics.

claim: Chromatin remodeling enzymes can move nucleosomes away or towards the factor binding sites to respectively enhance or inhibit factor binding.
source: Chromatin remodeling enzymes can move nucleosomes away or towards the factor binding sites to respectively enhance or inhibit factor binding.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromatin remodeling function.

claim: Cas9 activity can benefit from chromatin remodeling to access nucleosomal DNA.
source: We find that Cas9 activity can also benefit from chromatin remodeling to access nucleosomal DNA, as evidenced by the strong enhancements of Cas9 cleavage resulting from the action of the chromatin remodelers SNF2h and RSC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: SNF2h and RSC produce distinct nucleosomal arrangements yet still substantially alleviate nucleosome-mediated occlusion of Cas9 activity.
source: These two remodelers produce distinct nucleosomal arrangements yet still substantially alleviate nucleosome-mediated occlusion of Cas9 activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing both remodelers enhance Cas9 activity despite different mechanisms.

claim: In vivo, the majority of nucleosomes are not located on strong positioning sequences, and therefore may be permissive to Cas9 binding, especially at target sites that are readily accessible by DNA unpeeling.
source: In vivo, the majority of nucleosomes are not located on strong positioning sequences, and therefore may be permissive to Cas9 binding, especially at target sites that are readily accessible by DNA unpeeling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and knowledge of in vivo chromatin.

claim: Chromatin remodeling activities can provide diverse mechanisms to potentiate Cas9 activity at sites located close to the nucleosomal dyad or within more strongly positioned nucleosomes.
source: Chromatin remodeling activities can further provide diverse mechanisms to potentiate Cas9 activity at sites located close to the nucleosomal dyad or within more strongly positioned nucleosomes, which would otherwise be refractory to Cas9 action.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data with remodelers.

claim: The combination of spontaneous DNA unpeeling and remodeling contributes to the widespread success of CRISPR-Cas9 in eukaryotic cells.
source: We hypothesize that the combination of spontaneous DNA unpeeling and remodeling contributes to the widespread success of CRISPR-Cas9 in eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: Most applications of CRISPR-Cas9 in vivo have focused on genome engineering of protein-coding genes and other functional genomic elements associated with gene expression, which are typically associated with high rates of nucleosome remodeling.
source: Interestingly, most applications of CRISPR-Cas9 in vivo have focused on genome engineering of protein-coding genes and other functional genomic elements associated with gene expression, which are typically associated with high rates of nucleosome remodeling (Clapier and Cairns, 2009).
evidence: This is an observation about CRISPR applications supported by citation about remodeling at active genes.

claim: Cas9 can temporarily gain access to less accessible regions of the genome during specific points of cell cycle (e.g. DNA replication), leading to sufficient DNA cleavage events to promote NHEJ-mediated mutagenesis or HDR-mediated DNA integration at appreciable rates.
source: It is also conceivable that Cas9 can temporarily gain access to less accessible regions of the genome during specific points of cell cycle (e.g. DNA replication), leading to sufficient DNA cleavage events to promote NHEJ-mediated mutagenesis or HDR-mediated DNA integration at appreciable rates.
evidence: This is speculation about how Cas9 might access heterochromatin.

claim: Cas9 favors more accessible euchromatin regions but is not completely excluded from transcriptionally silent heterochromatin.
source: Recent studies on Cas9's behavior by single molecule imaging have also demonstrated that Cas9 favors more accessible euchromatin regions but is not completely excluded from transcriptionally silent heterochromatin (Knight et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a single molecule imaging study.

claim: For CRISPR applications that require stable binding of nuclease-deficient dCas9 to DNA, such as transcriptional regulation and live-cell imaging with fluorescent dCas9, even modest nucleosome phasing could have a dramatic impact.
source: For other CRISPR applications that require stable binding of nuclease-deficient dCas9 to DNA, such as transcriptional regulation and live-cell imaging with fluorescent dCas9, even modest nucleosome phasing could have a dramatic impact (Gilbert et al., 2013; Mali et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and citations to dCas9 applications.

claim: The +1 nucleosome in RNA pol II-transcribed genes is strongly positioned with phasing that dissipates gradually with each following nucleosome.
source: For example, the +1 nucleosome in RNA pol II-transcribed genes is strongly positioned with phasing that dissipates gradually with each following nucleosome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about nucleosome positioning at genes.

claim: The +1 nucleosome and resulting nucleosome phasing can exert a strong influence on dCas9's DNA-binding ability for transcriptional regulation, but the effect is less striking on genome editing with Cas9.
source: Several high resolution studies conducted in parallel to our work have established that the +1 nucleosome and resulting nucleosome phasing can exert a strong influence on dCas9's DNA-binding ability for transcriptional regulation, but the effect is less striking on genome editing with Cas9 (Horlbeck et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to parallel studies.

claim: sgRNA design strategies that avoid targeting near the dyad of strongly phased nucleosomes are likely to be more successful than current methods.
source: Our observations suggest that sgRNA design strategies that avoid targeting near the dyad of strongly phased nucleosomes are likely to be more successful than current methods.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Large scale nucleosome positioning or DNA accessibility maps are now readily available and can inform CRISPR sgRNA design in order to avoid targeting regions of low accessibility.
source: Large scale nucleosome positioning or DNA accessibility maps are now readily available and can inform CRISPR sgRNA design in order to avoid targeting regions of low accessibility (Jiang and Pugh, 2009; Thurman et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2014; Hsieh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a suggestion supported by citations to available genomic resources.

claim: Whole cell chromatin de-condensation or de-repression using chromatin factor drugs such as HDAC or DNA methyltransferase inhibitors may be an alternative and attractive strategy for improving CRISPR-Cas9 activity towards densely compact regions of chromatin.
source: Alternatively, whole cell chromatin de-condensation or de-repression using chromatin factor drugs such as HDAC or DNA methyltransferase inhibitors may be an alternative and attractive strategy for improving CRISPR-Cas9 activity towards densely compact regions of chromatin (Haaf, 1995; Tóth et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a suggestion supported by citations to chromatin decondensation studies.

claim: Remodelers from the SWI/SNF class have multiple outcomes, which include generation of DNA loops and eviction of the histone octamer in addition to nucleosome sliding.
source: While the ISWI remodeler SNF2h predominantly slides nucleosomes, remodelers from the SWI/SNF class have multiple outcomes, which include generation of DNA loops and eviction of the histone octamer in addition to nucleosome sliding (Rowe and Narlikar, 2010; Narlikar et al., 2001; Lorch et al., 1998; Schnitzler et al., 1998; Clapier and Cairns, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on SWI/SNF remodelers.

claim: SNF2h predominantly slides nucleosomes.
source: While the ISWI remodeler SNF2h predominantly slides nucleosomes, remodelers from the SWI/SNF class have multiple outcomes, which include generation of DNA loops and eviction of the histone octamer in addition to nucleosome sliding (Rowe and Narlikar, 2010; Narlikar et al., 2001; Lorch et al., 1998; Schnitzler et al., 1998; Clapier and Cairns, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SNF2h function.

claim: SNF2h slides the nucleosome enough to improve Cas9's accessibility to the target site.
source: Remodeling 80/0 nucleosomes by SNF2h resulted in a strong enhancement of Cas9 cleavage to ~34%, showing that SNF2h slides the nucleosome enough to improve Cas9's accessibility to the target site and that Cas9 is now able to bind and cleave at a higher rate (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: SNF2h remodels 80/0 end-positioned nucleosomes in a range of nucleosome positions biased towards the center of the DNA molecule.
source: SNF2h remodels 80/0 end‐positioned nucleosomes in a range of nucleosome positions biased towards the center of the DNA molecule, whereas RSC has the opposite bias of repositioned centered nucleosomes towards the ends of the DNA molecule.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: RSC has the opposite bias of repositioned centered nucleosomes towards the ends of the DNA molecule.
source: SNF2h remodels 80/0 end‐positioned nucleosomes in a range of nucleosome positions biased towards the center of the DNA molecule, whereas RSC has the opposite bias of repositioned centered nucleosomes towards the ends of the DNA molecule.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: RSC can destabilize nucleosome structure and reposition nucleosomes towards the DNA ends.
source: RSC can destabilize nucleosome structure and reposition nucleosomes towards the DNA ends.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Cas9 cleavage is substantially enhanced by RSC, attaining ~63% of the naked DNA cleavage rate.
source: Cas9 cleavage is substantially enhanced by RSC, attaining ~63% of the naked DNA cleavage rate.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: SNF2h improves Cas9 cleavage to ~35% of the naked DNA cleavage rate.
source: SNF2h improves Cas9 cleavage to ~35% of the naked DNA cleavage rate.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Simultaneous addition of SNF2h and Cas9 results in similar rate enhancement as sequential remodeling and cleavage.
source: We also performed this experiment by simultaneously adding SNF2h and Cas9 and found a similar rate enhancement (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: SNF2h improves Cas9 cleavage to ~40% of the naked DNA cleavage rate in simultaneous remodeling and cleavage assays.
source: SNF2h improves Cas9 cleavage to ~40% of the naked DNA cleavage rate, similarly to sequential remodeling and cleavage assays shown in Figure 3A–D.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.
